name: Syl Johnson
hook: A Chicago soul singer who called himself 'the most sampled man in history,' and had the sample databases to back it up.
blurb: Born Sylvester Thompson in Mississippi, Johnson moved to Chicago as a child, where the blues guitarist Magic Sam was his neighbour. He recorded Chicago soul for Twinight Records from 1966 to 1971 and then Memphis soul for Hi Records under Willie Mitchell from 1971 to 1977. His lasting influence on this map runs through a single drum break: his 1967 single 'Different Strokes', sampled by dozens of hip-hop acts from the earliest sample-based records on, including Wu-Tang Clan, Public Enemy and De La Soul. Later in his career he pursued sample-clearance and royalty claims hard, and spoke out for paying sampled artists.
